_comment: Golden cross-language vector for the veil.edge_event.v1 wire contract, ECDSA-P256/SHA-256 path (ADR-S, veil-custodian's per-device telemetry signing-key issuance). Sibling of edge_event_v1_golden.json (the HMAC vector) -- same wire contract, different SigningCredential. A downstream Python verifier must reproduce `canonical_json` byte-for-byte from `input`, using json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) for canonicalization (identical recipe to the HMAC vector) with integrity.signature set to the empty string "" during signing. Verification (NOT regeneration -- see the note on determinism below) with Python's `cryptography` library: `ec.derive_private_key(int(signing_key_scalar_hex, 16), ec.SECP256R1()).public_key().verify(utils.encode_dss_signature(int(signature_hex[:64], 16), int(signature_hex[64:], 16)), canonical_json.encode('utf-8'), ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))`. `signature_hex` is NOT DER -- it is fixed-width raw r||s (32-byte r, 32-byte s, big-endian, concatenated -- 64 bytes / 128 hex chars total), chosen so the wire format has exactly one valid encoding per signature (DER admits more than one for the same value); `utils.encode_dss_signature(r, s)` converts to DER first, which `verify()` requires. Determinism note: this signature was produced by Rust's `p256`/`ecdsa` crates, whose `SigningKey::sign` defaults to RFC 6979 deterministic nonce generation. Standard Python `cryptography` does NOT expose an RFC-6979 deterministic-ECDSA mode as of this writing -- `ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256())` there uses a randomized nonce, so calling `.sign(...)` in Python will NOT reproduce these exact bytes, only produce a different, equally-valid signature over the same message. This fixture is regenerated by re-running the Rust production path (`cargo test edge_event_v1_ecdsa_golden_vector_matches_the_fixture -- --nocapture` against a placeholder, then transcribing the printed values), never by hand or from Python. Pinned by crates/vg-core/tests/telemetry.rs's `edge_event_v1_ecdsa_golden_vector_matches_the_fixture` test, which reconstructs this exact record in Rust via the production AuditEvent -> EdgeEvent::try_from_audit_event -> sign_edge_event_record path (this time with SigningCredential::EcdsaP256) and asserts byte-exact equality against canonical_json and signature_hex below. This is the vector ADR-S's own text names as veilgremlin's owed follow-on: the preimage is this crate's own envelope-canonicalisation artifact, not something veil-custodian's API contract could correctly produce -- see that repo's docs/api/fixtures/signing-keys/README.md for the corresponding correction.

input._comment: The AuditEvent this record was built from, plus every value sign_edge_event_record needed. Deliberately identical audit_event/actor_pseudonym_key_hex to edge_event_v1_golden.json's own input -- the only thing this vector varies is the signing credential (ECDSA device key instead of HMAC), not a second, incidental difference. certificate_der_hex is a placeholder (not a real certificate) that DeviceSigningCredential::from_parts hashes to derive key_ref -- this test constructs a credential directly, the same way vg-core's own unit tests do, not through vg-vault's certificate parser (that derivation is covered by vg-core's KeyRef::from_certificate_der unit test and vg-vault's cross-repo one against the vendored custodian fixture).
